newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais round up illegal workers bound for Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Thais round up illegal workers bound for Malaysia.

text.p: Immigration officials in southern Thailand said on Friday they had rounded up 270 Bangladeshis and eight Indians who had entered the country illegally and were suspected of planning to sneak into Malaysia to find work.
The illegal immigrants were picked up in Sadao district of Songkla province bordering Malaysia on Thursday, a Sadao-based immigration officer told Reuters by telephone.
They would be sent to Bangkok and deported, he said.
Those arrested had arrived in Thailand two to three weeks ago and were believed to have used fake visas to enter the country, he added.
The Thai action follows Malaysia's recent charge that illegal workers, especially from Bangladesh and India, were using Thailand as a transit point to enter Malaysia illegally.
Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn, who visited Malaysia this week, pledged to curb the influx of illegal aliens during talks with his Malaysian counterpart.
But the Thai immigration official added that they would push back illegal workers coming into Thailand from Malaysia.
"We are closely monitoring the border and will push back all illegal entrants," he said.
Thailand's National Security Council estimated about 5,000 Bangladeshis, Burmese and Indians were hiding in the jungles along the border between Thailand and Malaysia.
"We are continuing to round up and deport these people but it will take sometime because we have a very limited budget," the Thai official said.
